subject: Archaeology
title: Alexandria's Sunken Royal Quarter
description: A short lesson to help you apply Alexandria's Sunken Royal Quarter.

hook.text: Cleopatra's royal palace lies underwater in the harbor of Alexandria.

buildup.text: Franck Goddio began mapping the site in 1996 and found columns, sphinxes, and statues scattered across the harbor floor.

discovery.text: A colossal granite statue of a Ptolemaic pharaoh was raised from the mud, standing over 16 feet tall.

twist.text: The famous Lighthouse of Alexandria — one of the Seven Wonders — also collapsed into the harbor.

climax.text: Egypt plans an underwater museum where visitors can view the ruins through glass tunnels beneath the harbor.

punchline.text: Cleopatra's palace is 20 feet underwater. Egypt plans to let visitors walk.

quiz.question: What caused Alexandria's royal quarter to sink?
options: Rising sea levels gradually flooded the coastline
Earthquakes dropped the structures into the harbor about 1,600 years ago
A tsunami from a volcanic eruption destroyed the foundations

details.summary: Earthquakes and subsidence dropped ancient Alexandria's royal quarter into the Mediterranean, where French archaeologist Franck Goddio mapped it in the 1990s. Submerged palaces, temples, Cleopatra's palace complex, and colossal statues of pharaohs now lie in the waters of the Eastern Harbour.
details.whyItMatters: Alexandria was the greatest city of the ancient world, yet its most important district lies underwater. Goddio's work revealed the physical layout of Ptolemaic power, placing Cleopatra's world in concrete archaeological rather than literary context.
takeaways: Alexandria's royal quarter sank into the harbour due to earthquakes
Franck Goddio mapped submerged palaces and temples in the 1990s
The discoveries include parts of Cleopatra's palace complex

faq.question: Can divers visit the sunken royal quarter?
faq.answer: Limited diving tours have been offered, but murky harbour water and active port traffic restrict access. Plans for an underwater museum have been proposed repeatedly but face funding and engineering challenges. Most visitors experience the finds through museum exhibitions of recovered artifacts.

faq.question: What has been found underwater in Alexandria?
faq.answer: Colossal granite statues, sphinx figures, column bases from palaces and temples, and the foundations of buildings matching ancient descriptions of the royal quarter. The remains of a shipwreck and ancient harbour infrastructure have also been documented in the Eastern Harbour.
